---
title: "Your own tiles and services"
---

Besides named basemaps and MapLibre styles, a style can be tile data: a tile
URL template, a TileJSON, a PMTiles archive (URL or local file), or an
ArcGIS service. basemapper detects whether the tiles are raster or vector
and builds a style for them. The source helpers `tiles()`, `provider()`,
`wms()` and `wmts()` take each source's own options, inside `style()`.

```{python}
import basemapper as bm
```

## A tile URL

An XYZ template, as raster tiles:

```{python}
bm.basemap("https://tile.opentopomap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", center=(-111.65, 40.60), zoom=11,
           width=720, height=405)
```

## PMTiles

A [PMTiles](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/) archive is read with HTTP
range requests, or from a local file. Raster archives draw as they are;
here a USGS topographic map of Mount Whitney, its extent given:

```{python}
bm.basemap("https://pmtiles.io/usgs-mt-whitney-8-15-webp-512.pmtiles",
           bounds=[-118.3198, 36.5611, -118.2607, 36.5930], width=720, height=405)
```

Vector archives get a default style over every source layer:

```{python}
firenze = "https://pmtiles.io/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles"
bm.basemap(firenze, center=(11.255, 43.773), zoom=13.5, width=720, height=405)
```

`tiles()` sets which source layers it draws, and their paint:

```{python}
print(sorted({l["source_layer"] for l in bm.list_layers(firenze)}))

styled = bm.style(bm.tiles(
    firenze,
    source_layers=["earth", "water", "landuse", "roads", "buildings"],
    paint={"fill-color": "#f2efe9", "line-color": "#8a8a8a"},
))
bm.basemap(styled, center=(11.255, 43.773), zoom=13.5, width=720, height=405)
```

### With a basemap style

A vector archive can also be drawn with a full basemap style whose source
points at it. [protomaps-light.json](../../styles/protomaps-light.json) and
[protomaps-dark.json](../../styles/protomaps-dark.json) are the
[Protomaps](https://github.com/protomaps/basemaps) basemap styles with the
Florence archive as their source
(`"url": "pmtiles://https://pmtiles.io/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles"`),
and a style file's path works as a style:

```{python}
def florence(s):
    return bm.basemap(s, center=(11.2551, 43.7710), zoom=15.2, width=720, height=405)

florence("styles/protomaps-light.json")
```

```{python}
florence("styles/protomaps-dark.json")
```

For your own Protomaps archive, change the source's `url` to `pmtiles://`
and the archive's URL or path. These styles are for Protomaps tiles v3;
archives built from late 2024 on use tiles v4, with the styles of
`@protomaps/basemaps` 5 ([how the styles were made](../../styles/README.md)).

## TileJSON

A TileJSON URL works the same way; this is OpenFreeMap's planet tileset,
with the default vector style:

```{python}
bm.basemap("https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet", center=(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom=12,
           width=720, height=405)
```

## Your tiles in a basemap's style

`provider(name, tiles=)` keeps a catalogue basemap's style and swaps in your
own tiles, which must use the same schema (OpenFreeMap's styles use
OpenMapTiles): self-hosted tiles, or an extract for offline use.

```{python}
own = bm.style(bm.provider("OpenFreeMap.Positron", tiles="https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet"))
bm.basemap(own, center=(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom=12, width=720, height=405)
```

## OGC services

`wms()` and `wmts()` take a service's parameters. Shaded relief from
terrestris's OpenStreetMap WMS:

```{python}
relief = bm.style(bm.wms("https://ows.terrestris.de/osm/service", layers="SRTM30-Colored-Hillshade"))
bm.basemap(relief, bounds=[-130, 20, -60, 55], width=720, height=360)
```

## In plots

Any of these goes in a plot:

```{python}
import geodatasets
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

nc = gpd.read_file(geodatasets.get_path("geoda.sids"))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.4))
nc.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="black", linewidth=0.4)
ax.set_xlim(-84.4, -81.2)
ax.set_ylim(34.9, 36.6)
bm.add_basemap(ax, "https://tile.opentopomap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", alpha=0.8, crs=nc.crs)
ax.set_axis_off()
```

## Keys

Some services need a key. A catalogue basemap reads its own from the
environment (`CARTO_API_KEY`, `MAPTILER_API_KEY`, `STADIA_API_KEY`,
`UGRC_QUAD_WORD`); any style takes one with `key`, sent only to that style's
own server:

```{python}
#| eval: false
import os
bm.style("MapTiler.Streets", key=os.environ["MAPTILER_API_KEY"])
bm.style("https://example.com/private/style.json", key="my-token")
```

## Tile cache

Tiles are cached on disk, for as long as the servers' caching headers
allow. `tile_cache()` shows where; `tile_cache(clear=True)` empties it, and
`tile_cache(False)` turns it off for the session.
